title: Algebraicity and smoothness of the stack of line bundles
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat proper morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Define a category $\mathcal B_f$ over $S$-schemes by taking its fibre over $T\to S$ to be the groupoid of invertible $\mathcal O_{X_T}$-modules and their isomorphisms [def-sc-invertible-module], where $X_T=X\times_ST$ [def-pc-base-change]. An arrow over $u:T'\to T$ is an isomorphism $u_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ for line bundles $L$ on $X_T$ and $L'$ on $X_{T'}$; pullback and composition are the usual pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\mathcal B_f$ is an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. If every fibre of $f$ has Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $\mathcal B_f\to S$ is smooth, in the sense that it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas whose composite with $\mathcal B_f\to S$ is smooth. No hypothesis on $f_*\mathcal O_X$, no section, no smoothness of $f$, and no reducedness of the fibres are required.

source.place: Tag 0D04, proposition-pic; literature/stacks-project/moduli.tex Tag 0DPJ, lemma-pic-curves-smooth (using Tag 0DMB, lemma-pic-qs-lfp).

proof.text: Properness includes separatedness, so form the coherent-family category $\mathcal C_f$ of [lem-sfb-coherent-stack-algebraic-lfp]. It is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$. The forgetful functor from the line-bundle category $\mathcal B_f$ is the representable open immersion of [lem-sfb-invertible-open-in-coherent-stack]: it has exactly the same objects, pullback isomorphisms and composition as the line-bundle category in that statement. Apply [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp] to this functor. Thus $\mathcal B_f$ is algebraic and its structural morphism is locally of finite presentation. This proves algebraicity without the relative dimension assumption.

source.place: Tag 0D04, proposition-pic, proof; moduli.tex Tag 0DMB, lemma-pic-qs-lfp.

proof.text: Now assume every fibre has dimension at most one. Take any first order thickening $T\hookrightarrow T\prime$ of affine $S$-schemes and any line bundle $L$ on $X_T$. Set $X\prime=X\times_ST\prime$ and $X_0=X_T$, with $g:X_0\to T$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], applied to schemes viewed as their representable algebraic spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], both base-changed families are flat, proper and of finite presentation. Their fibre dimensions are at most one by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change]: for a point $x\prime$ of a fibre of $g$, with image $x$ in the fibre $X_s$ of $f$, $\dim_{x\prime}=\dim_x(X_s)\le\dim X_s\le1$, since $X_s$ is itself an open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-kun-dimension]. A chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_n$ of irreducible closed subsets of the base-changed fibre meets every open neighbourhood $U$ of a point $x\prime\in Z_0$ in a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $U$, as each $Z_i$ is the closure of the nonempty open $Z_i\cap U$; hence $n\le\dim_{x\prime}\le1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-first-order-thickening-base-change], $X_0\hookrightarrow X\prime$ has square-zero ideal $I$. Its ideal is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. As an $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module it is still quasi-coherent: on a chart with ring $B$ and ideal $J$, $J^2=0$ makes $J$ a $B/J$-module, and $J\otimes_B B/J=J/J^2=J$.

source.place: Tag 0DPJ, lemma-pic-curves-smooth, affine thickening reduction; scheme base-change ideal as in more-morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-quasicoherent-fibre-dimension-vanishing] to $g:X_0\to T$, the quasi-coherent module $I$, and $d=1$. This gives $R^2g_*I=0$ without any Noetherian condition. Properness makes $g$ quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], so the affine-base comparison [lem-pc-cohomology-sections-affine-base] applies with $q=2$ and gives $H^2(X_0,I)\cong\Gamma(T,R^2g_*I)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E7D, lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre (1); coherent.tex Tag 01XK, lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images-application. This supplies the arbitrary-base vanishing in moduli.tex Tag 0DPJ.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-square-zero-picard-obstruction], the image of $\operatorname{Pic}(X\prime)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X_0)$ is the kernel of $\delta:\operatorname{Pic}(X_0)\to H^2(X_0,I)$. The last group is zero by step 3; hence $[L]$ lies in this image. A representative of a preimage is a line bundle $L\prime$ on $X\prime$ with an isomorphism $L\prime|_{X_0}\cong L$. Equality of Picard classes means precisely existence of this isomorphism, so it supplies the required arrow in the fibre groupoid, not merely a point in a sheafification.

The choice of affine $T\subset T\prime$ and $L$ was arbitrary, so step 4 proves essential surjectivity for every affine first order restriction functor of $\mathcal B_f$. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-infinitesimal-smooth-criterion] with local finite presentation established in step 1. It gives a smooth surjective scheme atlas whose structural composite to $S$ is smooth, exactly the smoothness required in the item.
